Auxiliary-loss-free balancing maintains an expert-specific bias used in routing selection. After measuring expert load, increase the bias of underused experts and decrease that of overloaded experts, nudging later selections toward balance. In DeepSeek-V3's described scheme, the selection bias is distinguished from the original affinity scores used to weight expert contributions. [1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.19437)

This avoids making a large balancing penalty directly distort the main-task gradient. It does not mean the entire training recipe has no auxiliary terms: the report also describes a complementary sequence-level balance objective. Bias-update magnitude and timing influence oscillation, specialization, and communication load. Track token/expert distributions, overflow, per-device load, and task loss. Balanced expert counts alone do not guarantee balanced wall-clock cost when experts or communication paths have unequal costs.
